A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same byte-level probability conversion work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original trained-model Markov-chain experiments, FIM code-completion evaluations, ensemble benchmarks and a beam-search ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds token-alignment and voting comparisons plus a stochastic-tokenization experiment in Appendix A.5.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 and ensemble averaging remain unchanged. Appendix E adds a proposed hybrid decoding option: generate bytes until whitespace, then switch to token generation with specified prompt-boundary constraints. Its use in the benchmark experiments is not reported.

E1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds trained-model evaluation on first-order A/B Markov sequences under stochastic, mixed-vocabulary tokenization, extending the empirical input conditions beyond v1's deterministic-tokenizer experiment. The existing FIM, knowledge, reasoning and coding benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Figure 6 adds token alignment from Athiwaratkun et al. (2024) to the SPM comparison. Table 1 adds top-2 voting on MMLU and PIQA. Existing token-healing and individual-model comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The new Appendix A.5 experiment uses transition parameters (alpha, beta) = (0.4, 0.3) and equally probable selection between vocabularies {A, B, AA} and {A, B}. Existing FIM prompt formats, temperature evaluation, pass@10 sampling and beam-search settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 adds a controlled investigation of whether stochastic tokenization eliminates bias, examining three token contexts and reconstructed byte probabilities. The beam-search ablation in Appendix C and three FIM generation case studies in Appendix D are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging 100 context evaluations for the third-order Markov experiment and retain Figure 6's shaded bands. v2 introduces no new run-count, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes Llama2-7B's GSM8K token/byte scores from 11.2/10.7 to 15.1/12.5 without explaining the revision. Added results include alignment's SPM greedy/pass@10 scores of 63.0/82.9, voting's MMLU/PIQA scores of 62.1/80.1, and Appendix A.5's probabilities. Existing proposed-method benchmark scores and Table 3 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly assumes zero probability for impossible encodings, restricts the invalid-encoding criterion to BPE/MPE, and refines the cover-encoding definition. It corrects alpha versus 1-alpha in the Markov example, asserts applicability to stochastic tokenizers, and adds a token-alignment counterexample in Appendix E. The central lemma and existing proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces its specific 1% advantage over token healing with a claim of correcting failure cases of both healing and alignment. The principal claims about zero-shot conversion, tokenization bias, 18% FIM improvement and up to 3.7% ensemble improvement remain.

C2.justification: Appendix A.5 adds explanations of partial bias mitigation under stochastic tokenization and inference of the vocabulary from context. Appendix E attributes alignment failures to greedy masking. Section 6.2 newly qualifies voting's applicability to reasoning tasks; existing memory, computation and theoretical limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project code-repository link in the abstract, absent from v1. Appendix A.5 also specifies the vocabulary mixture and transition parameters for its new experiment. The PDFs alone do not establish the repository's contents or functionality.

R1.justification: v2 adds Athiwaratkun et al. (2024) on token alignment and Provilkov et al. (2020) on BPE-dropout, discussing their relationship to tokenization bias. The broader related-work positioning and existing references are retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized rewrites in the introduction, mathematical explanations and conclusion, adds acknowledgments and two appendix sections, and updates the publication header. The main narrative and section ordering remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 6's table gains an alignment row and additional boldface, while Table 1 gains a voting row. Captions are revised, and Algorithm 3 and code listings are reflowed. The existing plots and beam-search table are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: Added alignment and voting comparisons, clearer mathematical assumptions and a code-access link strengthen validation and reproducibility information. These gains are limited but outweigh a localized problem in new Appendix A.5: its displayed probabilities imply alpha approximately 0.410 rather than the reported 0.405. That discrepancy weakens the example's precision without overturning its qualitative finding or the retained benchmark evidence.
